name: Helix Biosystems Subdermal Pressure Lattice
description:
The Subdermal Pressure Lattice is Helix Biosystems' most controversial commercial product — a surgically implanted armor system consisting of a network of flexible carbon-titanium filaments and pressure-distributing gel nodes installed beneath the skin across the torso, shoulders, and upper extremities. Unlike external armor, the SPL cannot be removed without surgery, provides no visible indication of protection, and functions by redistributing kinetic impact energy across the entire implanted network rather than stopping it at a surface layer. A bullet strike that would fracture bone and rupture tissue against unprotected skin instead compresses the gel nodes and transfers force laterally across the filament web, dramatically reducing penetration and localized trauma.

Helix markets the SPL primarily as a 'lifestyle protection solution' for corporate executives, high-value personnel, and individuals who require protection but cannot visibly appear to be wearing armor. The implantation procedure takes approximately six hours, requires a three-week recovery period, and must be performed by a licensed Helix biosurgical technician. The lattice is designed to last approximately seven years before requiring replacement or recalibration due to material fatigue and biological integration drift. Unauthorized implantation using black-market filament stock is known to cause severe inflammatory responses and in some cases fatal embolism.

The SPL occupies a deeply contested legal and ethical space in Meridian 88. Proponents argue it is a medical device and falls under body autonomy protections. Critics — primarily competing armor manufacturers and civil liberties groups — argue that it creates an invisible class of protected individuals who pass through security screening as unarmored civilians. Several jurisdictions within Meridian 88 have attempted to require SPL disclosure at checkpoints, with limited enforcement success.

cultural_context: In Meridian 88's upper corporate strata, having the SPL is a quiet signal of status — you can afford both the surgery and the implied threat level that justifies it. Among intelligence operatives and deep-cover agents, it is considered standard equipment for long-duration infiltration assignments. There is a growing underground market for SPL removal services catering to individuals who received implants under corporate employment contracts and want them out after leaving — Helix's standard contracts include clauses that technically classify the implants as company property.
story_hooks: A Helix biosurgeon has gone missing after performing unauthorized SPL removals for former corporate employees — Helix's recovery team is looking for her, and so are the people she helped.

A new black-market SPL variant using substandard filament stock is being implanted in street-level clients — the failure rate under sustained impact is causing internal hemorrhaging weeks after the fact.

A murder victim was found with no visible armor but survived three shots before the fourth killed them — the SPL signature in the autopsy has opened a jurisdictional nightmare about whether the killer knew they were shooting an armored target.

Helix's seven-year replacement clause is being enforced aggressively — clients who can't afford the replacement procedure are being threatened with remote filament contraction, which Helix claims is a 'safety feature' for expired lattices.
